text: Last night in the only home he's ever had. His mother won't sit down. His father is holding something wrapped in cloth, and won't quite meet his eyes.

speaker: Mother
text: Kai. Before you go, there's a thing we should have told you a long time ago. A thing we were always going to tell you tomorrow.

speaker: Kai
text: That's a lot of tomorrows, Mum.

speaker: Father
text: We found you. In the forest — that same stretch, sixteen years back. A baby, alone, no one for miles. And a sword laid down beside you, near as long as you were.

speaker: Mother
text: You are our son. That has never once been a question, not for a single day. We didn't tell you because — because we were afraid. That you'd feel less ours. That you'd go looking for where you came from and not come back.
His father unwraps the cloth. The old sword. The one that went warm in the dark.

speaker: Father
text: It was yours before it was anything of ours. It's time you had it. Whatever it means. Whatever you are.

speaker: Kai
text: I don't— I don't know what to do with any of this.

speaker: Kai
text: You could have told me. Any of the tomorrows, you could have just told me.

speaker: Mother
text: I know, love. I know. We're sorry. And we love you. Both of those are true, and neither one cancels the other.
